reference.title: Error Codes
reference.shortdesc: HTTP status codes and PayPal error identifiers returned by the REST API, with resolution guidance.

section.title: Error Response Structure
section.p: All PayPal API errors return a consistent JSON body:

row.entry: Malformed JSON or missing required field. Check the request body.
Field value is out of allowed range or wrong format (e.g., negative amount).
Invalid or expired access token. Refresh using POST /v1/oauth2/token.
The app does not have permission for this action. Check your app's feature entitlements in the dashboard.
The order or capture ID does not exist or belongs to a different environment (sandbox vs live).
PayPal-Request-Id reused with a different body. Use a unique ID per logical operation.
Business rule violation — e.g., capturing a non-approved order, refunding more than captured amount.
Cannot capture — buyer has not approved the order yet.
Buyer's payment method declined. Prompt buyer to use a different payment method.
Too many requests. Implement exponential backoff. Check Retry-After header.
Unexpected PayPal error. Retry with exponential backoff. Note the debug_id for support tickets.
PayPal is undergoing maintenance. Check PayPal Status.

note.p: Always log the debug_id field from error responses. When contacting PayPal Developer Support, include the debug_id so engineers can trace the exact request in PayPal's systems.
